CHINESE MEMBERS OF S.M.C. TO RESIGN(?) 


A report that Mr. Yu Ya Ching 
and four other Chinese members of the 8.M.C. will 
resign from the Council has come as a great shock to 
the public. The cause of their resignation is 
reported to be their dissatisfaction with the Council 
in dealing with the problem of the extra-Settlement 
roads area. 

The Chinese members of the 
S.M.C. appear to be dissatisfied with the Council 
because they were not invited to the Council meetings 
which were attended by the Japanese, British and 
American Councillors, and Mr. Phillips, Secretary and 
Commissioner-General, to discuss the problem of the 
extri-Settlement rords area. The fact that an outline 
for |ppettiement of the problem in question had been 
arawn7gnve rise to anxiety among the Chinese Councillors. 

On the morning of February 5 
Mr. Yu Ya Ching, when questioned by a reporter regarding 
his resignation, made the following statment:"It is true 
that we, the Chinese Councillors,intend to resign. We 
are considering the matter, but we have not yet come 
to a definite decision. From my own point of view 
we must exercise grest care in the matter. It does 
not mean I have any personal feeling about the minner 
in which the Council is handling the western aren problem. 
I am resolutely opposed to the reported outline of a 
solution of the problem. I am of the opinion that 
careful consideration of the problem is necessary."

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S.I. Special Branch
REPORT
Date December 12, 1940
Subject Report in the Tairiku Shinpo on alleged smuggling of arms
and ammunition by British Yacht
Made by D.S.I. MacAdie Forwarded by D. I. Crawford

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE REGISTRY No. 33 13-12-40 S.I. Special Branch）

With reference to the attached report
in the Tairiku Shimpo dated December 10th, 1940
and entitled 'British Yacht smuggles Arms and
Ammunition : Held by Water Police on Whangpoo River',
enquiries show that the report is greatly
exaggerated.

According to the Chinese Maritime Customs,
the yacht 'Kert' owned by W.D. Neil of Neil's
Bakery was taken without authority by the No. 2
Laodah for the purpose of smuggling cigarettes
to Tsungming Island. The craft was examined
by the Woosung Customs on December 9th and a
quantity of cigarettes was discovered as well
as a sporting rifle with ammunition for the same
and some rifle ammunition used for hunting purposes
and which is ordinarily kept on the boat by the
owner.

In the absence of Mr. W.D. Neil, a complaint
was lodged with the River Police by Mr. Hart,
the former's representative against the laodah
and the boat has been returned to the owner's
representative together with the gun and ammunition.
The laodah in question has been charged with the
larceny of the yacht in the Nantao District Court.

FILE

R.W. Mac Adie.
D. S. I.

主题 关于《大陆新报》报道英国游艇涉嫌走私军火弹药的报告
由副督察长 MacAdie 制作，由督察长 Crawford 转呈

（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处登记室 第33号 1940年12月13日 S.I. 特务科）

关于附上的1940年12月10日《大陆新报》题为“英国游艇走私军火弹药：在黄浦江被水警扣留”的报道，经查询显示，该报道严重夸大其词。

据中国海关称，尼尔面包店（Neil's Bakery）的 W.D. Neil 所有的游艇“Kert”号被二号老舵手擅自开走，目的是向崇明岛走私香烟。该船于12月9日接受吴淞海关检查，发现大量香烟，以及一支运动步枪和配套弹药，还有一些用于狩猎目的的步枪弹药，这些通常由船主存放在船上。

由于 W.D. Neil 先生不在，其代表 Hart 先生向水警投诉该老舵手，船只连同枪支和弹药已归还给业主代表。涉案老舵手已在南市地方法院被控盗窃游艇罪。

归档

R.W. Mac Adie.

February 6, 1940.
Afternoon Translation.

TAIRIKU SHIMPO

CHINESE MEMBERS OF S.M.C. TO RESIGN(?)

A report that Mr. Yu Ya Ching
and four other Chinese members of the S.M.C. will
resign from the Council has come as a great shock to
the public. The cause of their resignation is
reported to be their dissatisfaction with the Council
in dealing with the problem of the extra-Settlement
roads area.

The Chinese members of the
S.M.C. appear to be dissatisfied with the Council
because they were not invited to the Council meetings
which were attended by the Japanese, British and
American Councillors, and Mr. Phillips, Secretary and
Commissioner-General, to discuss the problem of the
extra-Settlement roads area. The fact that an outline
for a settlement of the problem in question had been
drawn up gave rise to anxiety among the Chinese Councillors.

On the morning of February 5
Mr. Yu Ya Ching, when questioned by a reporter regarding
his resignation, made the following statement:"It is true
that we, the Chinese Councillors, intend to resign. We
are considering the matter, but we have not yet come
to a definite decision. From my own point of view
we must exercise great care in the matter. It does
not mean I have any personal feeling about the manner
in which the Council is handling the western area problem.
I am resolutely opposed to the reported outline of a
solution of the problem. I am of the opinion that
careful consideration of the problem is necessary."

1940年2月6日。
下午译文。

《大陆新报》

工部局华董拟辞职(?)

有关虞洽卿先生及其他四位工部局华董将从公董局辞职的报道令公众大为震惊。据报道，他们辞职的原因是他们对公董局处理越界筑路区域问题感到不满。

工部局华董似乎对公董局感到不满，因为他们未被邀请参加由日、英、美籍董事以及秘书兼总办 Phillips 先生出席的讨论越界筑路区域问题的公董局会议。事实上，针对该问题的解决方案大纲已经拟定，这引起了华董们的焦虑。

2月5日上午，虞洽卿先生在接受记者关于其辞职的询问时，发表了如下声明：“我们华董打算辞职属实。我们正在考虑此事，但尚未做出最终决定。从我个人的角度来看，我们必须在此事上极为谨慎。这并不意味着我对公董局处理西区问题的方式有任何个人情绪。我坚决反对报道中提到的问题解决大纲。我认为有必要对该问题进行仔细考量。”

Relative to the attached news item appearing in
the "Tairiku Shimpo" of November 19, 1939 on the subject
of Shanghai's mosquito papers and their impending sale
to propaganda agents of the Chungking Government.

Many of the small publications are operating under
subsidy from either one of the two parties in the Chinese
political field and I know that efforts are being made to
intensify propaganda in Shanghai by both sides.

There has been no case of late coming to the notice
of this office wherein the Chungking Government has made
efforts to buy a mosquito paper; it is the usual thing
for the organ to be subsidised and a co-editor installed
by the people putting up the money.

19.11.29

MOSQUITO PAPERS WAIT FOR PROSPECTIVE PURCHASER

In view of the fact that a
number of mosquito newspapers in Shanghai are faced
with financial difficulty , the Chungking Government
has dispatched officers of its propaganda department
to Shanghai in order to purchase such mosquito papers
for the purpose of reviving anti-Japanese publications.
All mosquito newspapers are
reported to be waiting for Wang Ching Wei's party or
the Chungking Party it depends on who will pay the
greater subsidy.
The Wu Kwang Newsagency is
reported to be supplying anti-Wang Ching Wei news as the
result of a small subsidy from the Chungking Government.
This newsagency was established by Wu Soo Chung about 10
years ago to supply social news to small newspapers.

Shimpo
19.11.29

蚊子报等待潜在买家

鉴于上海多家蚊子报面临财务困难，重庆政府已派遣其宣传部官员前往上海，以便购买此类蚊子报，旨在复兴反日出版物。
据报道，所有蚊子报都在等待汪精卫派或重庆党，取决于谁提供更高的资助。
据报道，吴光通讯社因获得重庆政府的小额资助而提供反汪精卫的新闻。该通讯社由吴宿忠（Wu Soo Chung，音译）约10年前成立，旨在为小报提供社会新闻。

JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE TO SUPPRESS DISFIGURING
ADVERTISING POSTERS AND SIGNBOARDS IN HONGKEW.

Observing that a number of
advertising posters and hoardings harmful to the good
appearance of Hongkew have been put up recently, the Japanese
Consular Police started to suppress such advertisements
on September 18. Advertising posters are also being
freely affixed to telephone and electric poles as
well as on walls in a most disgraceful matter. Some of the
hoardings project considerably beyond the side walk.
A number of motor car owners who are without a garage are
parking their cars on the road outside their homes.

April 30, 1939. Morning Translation

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:

LABOUR DAY TO BE OBSERVED AS HOLIDAY BY LABOURERS
IN SHANGHAI.

To-morrow, May 1, being Labour Day, workers in
the employ of all local factories, mills, etc., will
observe it as a general holiday.
Owing to the extraordinary circumstances in
Shanghai, various labour organizations in Shanghai will
not do anything to commemorate the anniversary but the
labourers will be advised to work in harmony with their
employers and to endeavour through their labours to
render assistance in the war of resistance.
The "Shun Pao", the "Standard", the "Eastern
Times" and other local Chinese newspapers, in a notice,
announce that as Labour Day will be observed as a general
holiday by the workers, there will be no issue of these
newspapers on May 2, Tuesday.

"SIN SHUN PAO" AMALGAMATED WITH "TAIRIKU SHIMPO"

On April 29 the "Sin Shun Pao" (Japanese owned
Chinese language daily) announced in a notice that as
from to-day this paper has been amalgamated with the
"Tairiku Shimpo", a local Japanese language daily,
No. 455 Chapoo Road.

Standard (Evening Edition) dated April 29 :-

MOVEMENT OF WANG CHING-WEI

According to information secured from Hongkew,
Wang Ching-wei arrived at Shanghai two weeks ago and since
then he has been staying in a certain large building in
Hongkew. He has also interviewed certain Japanese high
officials.
Japanese War Minister Itagaki arrived at Shanghai
in a cruiser on April 26 and has been residing in the
Towa Hotel on Boone Road, the cruiser being berthed in
the Whangpoo River near Yangtszepoo. During the past few
days, General Itagaki and Wang Ching-wei have secretly
discussed certain terms and measures to form a puppet
Federal Government. General Itagaki has also invited
Wang to proceed to Tokyo in the same cruiser in a few days.
Information received from another source reveals
that the Japanese who arrived at Shanghai in the cruiser
on April 26 is General Tocho, the Director-General of the
Japanese Airforce, and not General Itagaki.

Hwa Mei Wan Pao dated April 29 :-

It is reported that Wang Ching-wei arrived at
Shanghai on April 24 and that certain results have been
achieved in secret conferences with the Japanese authorities.
However, it is generally believed that the report
that Wang is still staying in Hanoi is comparatively
reliable.

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COMMISSIONER'S OFF 1 MAY 1939）

上海劳工将劳动节定为假日。

明天，5月1日，正值劳动节，当地所有工厂、纱厂等雇佣的工人将将其作为普遍假日庆祝。
由于上海局势特殊，上海各劳工组织不会举行任何纪念活动，但会建议劳工与雇主和谐工作，并通过劳动努力协助抗战。
《申报》、《标准晚报》、《大公报》及其他本地中文报纸发布公告宣布，由于工人将劳动节作为普遍假日，这些报纸将于5月2日星期二停刊。

《新顺报》与《大陆新报》合并

4月29日，《新顺报》（日资中文日报）发布公告宣布，即日起该报与位于乍浦路455号的本地日文日报《大陆新报》合并。

4月29日《标准晚报》：-

汪精卫的动向

据从虹口获得的消息，汪精卫于两周前抵达上海，此后一直居住在虹口某座大型建筑内。他还会见了一些日本高级官员。
日本陆军大臣板垣于4月26日乘巡洋舰抵达上海，一直居住在布恩路（Boone Road，今长治路）的东亚酒店，该巡洋舰停泊在杨树浦附近的黄浦江上。在过去几天里，板垣将军与汪精卫秘密讨论了组建傀儡联邦政府的某些条款和措施。板垣将军还邀请汪在几天后乘坐同一艘巡洋舰前往东京。
来自另一来源的情报显示，4月26日乘巡洋舰抵达上海的是日本空军总监 Tocho 将军，而非板垣将军。

4月29日《华美晚报》：-

据报道，汪精卫于4月24日抵达上海，并与日本当局的秘密会议取得了一定成果。
然而，人们普遍认为，关于汪仍留在河内的报道相对可靠。

SHANGHAI TIMES.
JAN 3 1939

（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL S. B. REGISTRY No. S. B. D. 8933 Date 4 / 1 / 39）

Aims Set Out By Japanese
Daily In First Issue

“Tairiku Shimpo” Makes Appearance On New Year’s
Day; New Paper Is Merged With Shanghai
“Nippo”; To Push Japanese Aims

Displaying prominently extensive
messages of congratulation signed
by Prince Konoye and Japanese
Cabinet Ministers, General Shunroku
Hata, Commander-in-Chief of the
Japanese Expeditionary Force to
Central China; Vice-Admiral
Koshiro Oikawa, Commander-in-
Chief of the Japanese China Seas
Fleet, and other prominent Japan-
ese, the “Tairiku Shimpo,” a new
Japanese daily, made its first ap-
pearance here on New Year’s Day.
The first issue comprised 20 pages.

In an editorial, the new daily set
forth its two objectives. These were:
(1) To contribute towards Japan’s
destiny of expansion on the Asiatic
continent in pursuance of her his-
torical mission as the permanent
leader of East Asia, and
(2) To strive to deepen the mutual
understanding of Japan and China
for the rebirth and concord of all
Asiatic peoples through the pro-
motion and mixing of their cultural,
political and economic relations.

Long-Felt Need

“There has been a long-felt need
for the establishment of an authori-
tative news organ in this metropolis
of international importance so that
Japanese of all walks of life may
deepen their understanding of
China; to awaken the Chinese
masses from the nightmare of anti-
Japanism into which they were
driven by the misguided policy of
General Chiang Kai-shek’s military
clique, and to enable foreigners to
understand the truth and realize the
true intentions of Japanese policy,”
the editorial said.

“In answer to this urgent need,
deepened by the gravity of the
present situation, the ‘Tairiku
Shimpo’ has been established.”

The daily stressed the importance
of Shanghai as the “economic heart”
of China. It emphasized that the
position of this port would play a
major part in developing Japan’s
strong continental policy now being
put into effect.

The merger of the Shanghai
“Nippo,” the oldest Japanese lan-
guage periodical here, with the
“Tairiku Shimpo,” was also an-
nounced.

日文日报在首期阐明宗旨

《大陆新报》于元旦问世；新报与上海《日日新闻》合并；旨在推进日本目标

这份新的日文日报《大陆新报》于元旦在此间首次亮相，显著刊登了近卫公爵、日本内阁大臣、华中派遣军总司令畑俊六中将、中国方面舰队司令长官及川古志郎海军中将以及其他日本知名人士签署的大量贺词。首期共20版。

在社论中，该新日报阐明了其两大目标。即：(1) 秉承作为东亚永久领导者的历史使命，为日本在亚洲大陆的扩张命运做出贡献；以及 (2) 通过促进和融合文化、政治及经济关系，努力加深中日相互理解，以实现所有亚洲民族的复兴与和谐。

长期之需

社论称：“在这个具有国际重要性的大都市，长期以来一直需要建立一个权威的新闻机构，以便让各界日本人加深对中国的了解；将中国民众从蒋介石将军军事集团错误政策驱使他们陷入的反日噩梦中唤醒，并使外国人了解真相，认识到日本政策的真实意图。”

“为了回应这一因当前局势严峻而愈发迫切的需求，《大陆新报》应运而生。”

该日报强调了上海作为中国“经济心脏”的重要性。它强调，该港口的地位将在目前正付诸实施的日本强有力的大陆政策发展中发挥主要作用。

此外还宣布，上海历史最悠久的日文期刊《上海日日新闻》（Shanghai Nippo）将与《大陆新报》合并。

（批注：1月3日 798 1月6日）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
No. S. B. D. 8933
S. 1. Special Branch Section,
Date 3/ 12 38
Date December 31, 1938.

Subject Establishment of the Tairiku Shinpo, a Japanese daily, in
Shanghai.
Made by D. S. Kamashita Forwarded by C. Crawford.

The Tairiku Shinpo, a local Japanese daily, has
recently opened offices at No. 288 Seward Road and intend
circulating its first issue both morning and evening editions
on January 1, 1939. This new daily will absorb the
Shanghai Nippo, one of the leading local Japanese newspapers,
which has been existed since July, 1904, and the publication
of the Shanghai Nippo will cease from December 31, 1938.
Mr. Shunichi Fukuya(福家俊一) is stated to be the
President of the new establishment, while Mr. Shuji Uyeno
(上野祝二) will act as printer and publisher. The
editor in chief is reported to be Mr. Gisuke Kinoshita, who
was formerly special corespondent in Shanghai of the Osaka
and Tokyo Asahi Shimbun, one of the most influential dailies
in Japan. Beside Mr. Kinoshita several ex-employees of
the Osaka and Tokyo Asahi Shimbun will be granted important
positions in this new paper and in view of this fact it is
generally believed that there is a close connection with the
Osaka and Tokyo Asahi Shimbun.
The building housing the newspaper has a large hall
which is capable of accommodating several hundred persons
in addition to the various departments required in the
publication of a newspaper and the hall will be utilized for
public and private meetings.

主题 在上海设立日文日报《大陆新报》（Tairiku Shinpo）。
呈报人：D. S. Kamashita 转呈人：C. Crawford。

本地日文日报《大陆新报》（Tairiku Shinpo）最近在西华德路288号开设办事处，并计划于1939年1月1日发行首期早报和晚报。这家新日报将兼并当地主要日文报纸之一、自1904年7月以来一直存在的《上海日日新闻》（Shanghai Nippo），《上海日日新闻》将于1938年12月31日起停刊。据悉，新机构的社长为福家俊一先生（Shunichi Fukuya），上野祝二先生（Shuji Uyeno）将担任印刷人和出版人。据报道，主编为木下义助先生（Gisuke Kinoshita），他曾任日本最具影响力的日报之一《大阪朝日新闻》和《东京朝日新闻》驻上海特派记者。除木下先生外，几名《大阪朝日新闻》和《东京朝日新闻》的前雇员也将在这家新报纸中获得重要职位，鉴于这一事实，人们普遍认为其与《大阪朝日新闻》和《东京朝日新闻》有着密切联系。容纳该报社的建筑物设有一个大厅，除了报纸出版所需的各种部门外，该大厅可容纳数百人，并将用于公共和私人会议。

NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS,

DEC 3 1 1938

‘Shanghai Nippo’ Merges
With New Daily

“Tariku Shimpo” to Make
Bow Tomorrow

Bringing to an end a 34-year
history as a news organ serving the
local Japanese community, the
“Shanghai Nippo” appeared for the
last time here yesterday.
The suspension was a prelude to
its merger with the “Tariku Shimpo,”
a daily which will make its debut
on January 1. “Tairiku Shimpo” in
English means “Continental News.”
The “Tairiku Shimpo,” with
offices at 288 West Whatung Road,
will have morning and evening
editions. It will be a 12-page paper,
including both editions.
Mr. Shunichi Fukuya will be
chairman of the board of the new
daily, with Mr. Takeshi Kinoshita
as the chief editor. Mr. Takasni
Moriyama, former correspondent of
the Osaka and Tokyo “Asahi” news-
papers in Shanghai, will be managing
editor. Mr. Ryonosuke Toyokawa,
formerly of the “Osaka Mainichi”
chain of newspapers, will be one of
the associate editors.

《华北每日新闻》，

1938年12月31日

《上海日日新闻》与新日报合并

《大陆新报》将于明日亮相

《上海日日新闻》作为服务于本地日本社区的新闻机构，结束了其34年的历史，昨日在此间最后一次出版。
此次停刊是其与《大陆新报》（Tariku Shimpo）合并的前奏，后者将于1月1日首次发行。“Tairiku Shimpo”英文意为“大陆新闻”。
《大陆新报》办事处位于西华德路288号，将发行早报和晚报。包括两个版本在内，该报共12版。
福家俊一先生将担任新日报的董事会主席，木下武先生（Takeshi Kinoshita）任主编。前《大阪朝日新闻》和《东京朝日新闻》驻上海记者森山隆先生（Takasni Moriyama）将任执行编辑。原属《大阪每日新闻》报系的丰川龙之介先生（Ryonosuke Toyokawa）将任副编辑之一。
